household.name: fat, Korgfat, plate
household.title: fat, Korgfat, plate
household.reason: A finely twined basketry tray/plate with geometric zigzag and triangle designs, used as a gambling tray ("Korgfat, användes vid spel") — a classic Modoc/Klamath basin basketry form, consistent with the claimed Modoc ethnicity.

household.name: korg, basket
household.title: korg, basket
household.reason: The image shows a coiled/twined basket (bowl form), a household object consistent with Klamath-Modoc basketry traditions of the Cascade region; the museum record itself ties it to "Klamath-Modoc" peoples.

photo.name: photographic print; cabinet card
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); cabinet card
photo.reason: A studio cabinet-card portrait of Bogus Charley and Burgess Charley, identified Modoc men, captioned as "Modoc Indians, prisoners" certified by a U.S. Army officer at the time; this is a documentary photo of Modoc individuals, clothed in 19th-century American dress typical of the period.

photo.name: photographic print; cabinet card
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); cabinet card
photo.reason: This 1873 cabinet card is a documentary photograph of three Modoc men (identified as "Captain Jack's capturers"), including traditional dress elements like the embroidered/beaded cloth tied at the waist of the man on the left, alongside period Western clothing worn by the group.

photo.name: photographic print; cabinet card
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); cabinet card
photo.reason: Studio portrait of Scar Faced Charley, identified as a Modoc man, wearing a period three-piece suit and bow tie — a documentary photo of an identifiable Modoc individual.

photo.name: photographic print; cabinet card
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); cabinet card
photo.reason: This is a studio cabinet-card portrait of Bogus Charley, identified as a Modoc man, taken during his time as a prisoner/scout during the Modoc War era—a documentary photograph of an individual from the named people.

photo.name: photographic print; cabinet card
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); cabinet card
photo.reason: A studio cabinet-card portrait of Boston Charley, identified as a Modoc prisoner, documenting his dress and appearance; a documentary photograph of the named ethnicity qualifies.

garment.name: mössa, knit cap
garment.title: mössa, knit cap
garment.reason: The image shows a finely twined basketry cap with geometric zigzag designs, described as belonging to Modoc Captain Jack — basket hats of this type are characteristic traditional headwear of the Modoc/Klamath region.

garment.name: huvudbonad, hatt, headgear
garment.title: huvudbonad, hatt, headgear
garment.reason: This is a twined basketry cap ("squaw cap") with geometric patterning, a well-known woven hat form made and worn by Modoc and neighboring northern California groups. It fits the claimed ethnicity and category as a genuine garment/headwear item.

garment.name: mössa, Kvinnomössa, knit cap
garment.title: mössa, Kvinnomössa, knit cap
garment.reason: The image shows a twined basketry cap ("korgflätning" = basket weaving, "kvinnomössa" = woman's cap) with a geometric diamond pattern, a well-documented traditional headwear form worn by Modoc and neighboring Plateau/California women.

jewelry.name: smycke, halsband
jewelry.title: smycke, halsband
jewelry.reason: A necklace of glass beads and abalone shell pendants, documented as having belonged to Hi-ne-ma, a heroine of the 1873 (Modoc) war — direct attribution to a named Modoc individual supports the ethnicity claim, and shell/beadwork necklaces are consistent with Modoc/Plateau-Californian adornment.

jewelry.name: halsband, smycke
jewelry.title: halsband, smycke
jewelry.reason: A multi-strand necklace made of dark seeds/pits strung together, described as a "Halsband av frukter" (necklace of fruit/seeds) collected among the Modoc of the southern Cascades. This is a plausible traditional adornment for the claimed people.
